**Finding submitted: deviation on rule IP (Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found across the responsive locations:

- **§ 2(a)/(b)/(c)/(d) (p0022–p0029)** — the only IP allocation runs one way: we get a non-exclusive, use-and-execute licence to the Interface that lasts only "until this Agreement is terminated," and TrueLink "retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface."
- **§ 4 Support Services (p0043) / recital (p0004)** — TrueLink performs "programming customization services" we pay for under Exhibit "B", yet no clause allocates ownership of, or licences, the results of that work.
- **§ 10(b)/(c) (p0063, p0065)** — "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" are only deemed Client Proprietary Information, i.e. a confidentiality classification, not an ownership or licence right.
- **§ 8(d) (p0054)** — a non-exclusive licence (not an assignment) of narrowly defined aged raw Credit Data, excluding Client Proprietary Information; no walk-away trigger, so not flagged.
- **§ 13 (p0078)** and **§ 29 (p0096)** — we retain ownership of domains and Client Content on discontinuation, and no joint ownership is created anywhere.

Because there is no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence and no modify/sublicense rights over the work product created for us, the bargain fails the fallback on material terms. The redline is a single inserted § 2(e) targeting the fallback — TrueLink keeps the Interface and its tools/know-how (already met by § 2(d)), and we get the licence to the results of the Support Services. Validation returned ok:true with the minimality gate satisfied.
